name: Michael Gates
title: Republican nominee for California Attorney General (2026); former Huntington Beach City Attorney
years_of_service: Huntington Beach City Attorney 2014 to 2025 (elected 2014, 2018, 2022); U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division, deputy assistant attorney general, 2025. (Ballotpedia; San Joaquin Valley Sun)
background: Gates lives in Huntington Beach. He holds a bachelor's degree from Pepperdine and a law degree from Chapman University School of Law, and was a litigator and partner at an Orange County law firm before public office. (Ballotpedia)

Elected Huntington Beach City Attorney in 2014 and re-elected twice, he challenged what he called lenient state criminal-justice policy and fought state laws requiring the city to plan for more affordable housing. He defended the city's voter-ID ordinance against a lawsuit by Attorney General Bonta and Secretary of State Weber. (CalMatters; San Joaquin Valley Sun)

In 2025 he joined the Trump Justice Department's Civil Rights Division as a deputy assistant attorney general, where he said he helped file eight lawsuits seeking voter-registration files, including against Orange County. He resigned later that year to return to the Huntington Beach city attorney's office (one report says as chief assistant city attorney). He placed second in the June 2026 AG primary with 37.94%. (LAist; San Joaquin Valley Sun; Ballotpedia)
